paragraphs: Harmonize sells collaboration tools that higher education instructors run inside the learning management system they already use. The suite covers discussion, peer review, document annotation, and more. It works with any major LMS and, the company says, feels familiar enough that there is virtually no learning curve.

Discussion boards are multimedia enabled and come with Turnitin integration, multiple due dates, and auto grading. Social annotation moves the conversation into the document itself, by highlighting text and dropping pins. AI features generate captions, audio descriptions, and alt text on both instructor and student content. Instructors can also run polls, set up small groups, or enable anonymous posting. Engagement Insights is offered for reporting on student performance and for compliance with RSI guidelines.

The team says it has worked closely with educators since 2008. It started as 42 Lines, a custom development shop for higher education. The press page says the product reaches institutions from the University of Michigan to Piedmont Community College. Listed announcements include a partnership with the Oklahoma State Regents for Higher Education.

quote.text: There was a large gap between the kinds of discussion instructors wanted students to have online and the kind of discussions that happened.
